parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented universal-exposure measure (no facility rule, no border document friction recorded), and same-sex conduct decriminalised. Positives are documented: supreme court compelled recognition in 2008, a sterilisation condition rejected in 2009, civil unions in force, an openly gay head of government (2023), annual Pride, and asylum protection for LGBTI seekers. The main negatives are visitor-facing: a documented pattern of failed investigation/prosecution of identity-based violence (2020 attack downgraded to public order, regional court found violations in 2024; a second case police closed until the national prosecutor intervened — outcomes unresolved), leaving a trans assault victim thin recourse; no gender-identity anti-discrimination provision; and dated conservative religious hostility. Police treatment of trans people, border screening and facilities are open questions, not exposures. Nothing approaches tier-1 exclusion or organised targeting, so this sits in Reduced Risk, held below 0.75 by the impunity pattern and the thin trans-specific record.
